holidays.name: World Emoji Day
holidays.description: Today the whole world celebrates the little yellow faces, tiny tacos and dancing ladies that have taken over our texts. Send an emoji-only message, swap your favorites, or reply to a serious email with a single crying-laughing face.
holidays.origin: Emoji historian Jeremy Burge created World Emoji Day in 2014. He picked July 17 because that is the date shown on the calendar emoji in Apple's iOS design.
holidays.funFact: Emoji got their start in late-1990s Japan. Shigetaka Kurita designed the first set of 176 emoji, each only 12x12 pixels, and they are now part of the permanent collection at New York's Museum of Modern Art.

holidays.name: Yellow Pigs Day
holidays.description: This is a holiday for math nerds, and it celebrates an imaginary yellow pig. Fans mark it with yellow foods, pig-themed gatherings, and plenty of talk about the number 17.
holidays.origin: Yellow Pigs Day began in the mathematics community, with roots in a summer math program at Hampshire College. A mathematical in-joke about a yellow pig and the number 17 grew into an annual tradition, and it spread to math departments and campuses. Because the date is 7/17, the day is a tribute to 17.
holidays.funFact: The yellow pig tradition says every yellow pig has exactly 17 of something. Math fans love that 17 is a prime number, so it fits the joke.

holidays.name: Wrong Way Corrigan Day
holidays.description: This day honors the pilot who set off for California and landed in Ireland. It is a toast to wrong turns, happy accidents and total confidence in the face of a mistake.
holidays.origin: On July 17, 1938, aviator Douglas Corrigan took off from Brooklyn, New York, in a patched-up single-engine plane, with a flight plan for California. About 28 hours later he landed in Dublin, Ireland. He claimed a compass error and cloud cover had thrown him off course.
holidays.funFact: Corrigan had been refused permission for a transatlantic flight. He stuck to his story for the rest of his life, and he earned the nickname Wrong Way Corrigan.
